title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
oneLinerQuestion: Maximize profit by choosing a single day to buy a stock and a future day to sell it.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock problem asks for the maximum profit achievable from a single transaction (buying on one day and selling on a subsequent day). A brute-force evaluation of all pairs requires O(N^2) comparisons. Because you must buy before you can sell, the problem can be framed as: for each day, what is the maximum profit achievable if we sell today? The answer is simply today's price minus the lowest price seen on any preceding day. By tracking the running minimum price during a single linear sweep, we calculate potential profits dynamically in O(N) time and O(1) space.

- Step 1: Base Case & Edge Checking — If the prices array has 0 or 1 elements, no transaction can be completed (you cannot buy and sell on separate days), so the maximum profit is 0.

- Step 2: State Tracking Initialization — We initialize two primitive variables: 'minPrice = prices[0]' (representing the lowest purchase price observed so far) and 'maxProfit = 0' (representing the best profit realized across any transaction).

- Step 3: Single-Pass Linear Traversal — We iterate through the array starting from index 1 to prices.length - 1 with pointer 'i', treating prices[i] as the hypothetical sell price for that day.

- Step 4: Minimum Price Update — If prices[i] < minPrice, we update 'minPrice = prices[i]'. A cheaper purchase price cannot yield a profit on the current day, but it sets a better foundation for any future selling opportunities.

- Step 5: Potential Profit Calculation — If prices[i] >= minPrice, we calculate the profit if sold today: 'profit = prices[i] - minPrice'. We then update our global record: 'maxProfit = Math.max(maxProfit, profit)'.

- Step 6: Termination & Return — After traversing all available trading days, 'maxProfit' holds the maximum possible profit from a single buy-sell trade.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) because the array of prices is scanned in a single pass of length N. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space as only two scalar variables ('minPrice' and 'maxProfit') are maintained throughout execution.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION maxProfit(prices):
    minPrice = INFINITY, maxProf = 0
    FOR price IN prices DO:
        IF price < minPrice THEN minPrice = price
        ELSE IF price - minPrice > maxProf THEN maxProf = price - minPrice
    END FOR
    RETURN maxProf
END FUNCTION
